_comment: ONLY the delta over prolog/src/carriers.pl. carrier_name/2 already maps all sixteen member names and affiliate/3 the fourteen affiliates that hold their own designator, so restating either here would be a third copy of the vocabulary and the one that drifts. What is left is the spellings English Wikipedia's airport tables use that neither of those covers. prolog/test/test_network.pl asserts every designator this file can produce satisfies carriers:carrier_code/1, which is what stops the two halves diverging.
_aliases: An operator string naming exactly one operating certificate. The regional brands here -- QantasLink, Fiji Link, Royal Air Maroc Express, BA Euroflyer -- are the ones carriers.pl records as flying under the parent's own designator, so the parent's code is the operating carrier and not a guess.
_brands: A brand covering several operating certificates. PLANS/06 phase 2: where the table cannot say which one flew, the operating carrier is UNKNOWN and never a guess -- and an unknown operating carrier is not a carriers:carrier_code/1, so the row yields no fact and reaches services.rejects.json under operator_brand_ambiguous instead. 4(j) already degrades to a warning on an absent operating carrier; feeding it a wrong one is worse than feeding it nothing.
_excluded: Strings that resolve through one of the tables above but must not: a cargo or charter arm carrying the passenger airline's name, or a namesake that is a different company.
